title: Scheduling & Resources
summary: How Kubernetes decides where pods run and how much of a node they may use: requests and limits, throttling vs OOMKill, QoS, quotas, the scheduler's filter/score loop, affinity, taints, topology spread, priority, disruption budgets, and sizing Node.js containers correctly.
objectives: Explain requests vs limits and predict CPU throttling vs memory OOMKill
Identify a pod's QoS class and how it affects eviction
Enforce defaults and budgets per namespace with LimitRange and ResourceQuota
Describe how the scheduler filters and scores nodes, and debug Pending pods from scheduler events
Place pods with nodeSelector, node affinity, pod (anti-)affinity, taints/tolerations and topologySpreadConstraints
Use PriorityClasses, PodDisruptionBudgets, cordon and drain safely
Right-size containers with metrics-server and `kubectl top`, including Node.js heap vs container memory
